messages.subject: Ability to use diurnal burrow locations of marked individuals in secr to estimate density?
messages.subject_clean: Ability to use diurnal burrow locations of marked individuals in secr to estimate density?
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

I am doing research on a burrowing mammal (bilby) and have a question for the secr community.

I have limited trapping data for one of the populations I am studying, but I do have data on their diurnal burrow locations (from radio-tracking) for a more substantial period of time. Burrow sharing is not uncommon in bilbies, particularly between female and young at foot.

My question is, would it violate secr assumptions to use these diurnal burrow locations as 'traps' in secr ('single' traps capturing only the radio-tagged individual each time)?

I can appreciate this may be a stretch and not the typical input for secr, but I am keen to be able to estimate the density of this population despite the limited trapping data. Any suggestions are welcomed.

Thanks,
Cass

messages.subject: Re: Ability to use diurnal burrow locations of marked individuals in secr to estimate density?
messages.subject_clean: Ability to use diurnal burrow locations of marked individuals in secr to estimate density?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Cass
Here's my take, with the usual caveats that I don't have the full picture and others may disagree:
Your burrow data are really just a subsample of the telemetry locations of tagged individuals (assuming you didn't actually monitor burrows per se to see who used them at other times). That means the telemetry data have the strengths and peculiarities of  telemetry data in general: the estimate of scale from telemetry data may or may not match the scale of detection in traps, the relation between the telemetry sample and the trapped sample needs to be defined (see e.g.  Fig. 2 in https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-telemetry.pdf), and generally telemetry does not add much to SECR estimates of density. Estimation of density requires sampling the untagged animals, that by definition do not appear in the telemetry sample.
Murray

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for your reply Murray, just to confirm, you are suggesting the burrow locations from radiotracking are best used as telemetry data rather than treating them as a 'trapped' individual (in the absence of a large trapping data set)?

I do have some trapping data for a small number of traps (~25-30 traps, used several times each over a 2 week period) in which I captured both 'tagged' and 'untagged' animals. I have combined this with telemetry data from the tagged animals (ie concurrent telemetry data, 21 nights of tracking, 1 fix per night). I have thought this dataset may be too small to produce reliable results in secr, but I would appreciate thoughts on this.

Thanks,
Cass

messages.subject: Re: openCR 2.0.2
messages.body_plain:
That particular backward compatibility problem arises because openCR 2.0 added the details argument 'minimumage' and the function openCR.make.newdata did not allow for old models in which it wasn't defined. I think it would be fixed by inserting a value thus

oldfit$details$minimumage <- 0

As this shows, the code has not been tested for backward compatibility and there may be other issues. It's good to catch this now, and I'll run some other checks.

Murray

messages.subject: Problem with make.capthist in secr 4.4.4
messages.body_plain:
Hello

I encountered a problem while using make.capthist(), which appears to jumble up the trap and capture locations in the output. I don't think I have encountered this issue previously, but I haven't used make.capthist() in quite a while.

Code is as follows since I had problems attaching it:

library(secr)
library(spatstat)
# Make traps
nx <- 8
ny <- 8
trapSpacing <- 5000
traps <- make.grid(nx, ny, spacing=trapSpacing,
  detector='proximity')
# Make mask
simMask <- make.mask(traps, buffer=2e4)
A <- area(simMask) / 1e4
bbox <- attr(simMask, "boundingbox")
# Set biological parameters
N <- 20
( D <- N / A )  # animals / ha
# Set detection parameters
g0 <- 0.02
sigma <- 5000
nOcc <- 90
# Simulate capture history
set.seed(2359)
popn <- sim.popn(D=N / area(simMask) * 1e4, core=bbox,
model2d="poisson", Ndist="fixed")
rownames(popn) <- paste0("ID", sprintf("%02d",
as.numeric(rownames(popn))))
simCH <- sim.capthist(traps, popn=popn,
detectpar=list(g0=g0, sigma=sigma),
noccasions=nOcc, renumber=FALSE)
# Revert to capture file
simCF <- as.data.frame(simCH)
# Add xy coordinates
simCF$x <- traps$x[match(simCF$TrapID, rownames(traps))]
simCF$y <- traps$y[match(simCF$TrapID, rownames(traps))]
# Capthist with Trap ID
obsCH_TrapID <- make.capthist(simCF[,1:4], traps)
# Capthist with xy coordinates
obsCH_XY<- make.capthist(simCF[,-4], traps, fmt="XY")
# Plot capture histories
par(mfrow=c(1, 3))
plot(simCH, tracks=TRUE, rad=500)
plot(obsCH_TrapID, tracks=TRUE, rad=500)
plot(obsCH_XY, tracks=TRUE, rad=500)
# Fit models
fit_OG <- secr.fit(simCH, mask=simMask)
fit_TrapID <- secr.fit(obsCH_TrapID, mask=simMask)
fit_XY <- secr.fit(obsCH_XY, mask=simMask)

Thanks for any help or suggestions with this.

Yan Ru

Had another go at this, and it seems that the problem lies with as.data.frame when using fmt="trapID", whereas fmt="XY" seems to have no issues. Sorry for the misdirection and thanks to anyone who took a look. Here's the slightly modified code where using xy-coordinates instead of trap ID does not produce problems.

library(secr)
library(spatstat)
# Make traps
nx <- 8
ny <- 8
trapSpacing <- 5000
traps <- make.grid(nx, ny, spacing=trapSpacing,
  detector='proximity')
# Make mask
simMask <- make.mask(traps, buffer=2e4)
A <- area(simMask) / 1e4
bbox <- attr(simMask, "boundingbox")
# Set biological parameters
N <- 20
( D <- N / A )  # animals / ha
# Set detection parameters
g0 <- 0.02
sigma <- 5000
nOcc <- 90
# Simulate capture history
set.seed(2359)
popn <- sim.popn(D=N / area(simMask) * 1e4, core=bbox,
model2d="poisson", Ndist="fixed")
rownames(popn) <- paste0("ID", sprintf("%02d",
as.numeric(rownames(popn))))
simCH <- sim.capthist(traps, popn=popn,
detectpar=list(g0=g0, sigma=sigma),
noccasions=nOcc, renumber=FALSE)
# Revert to capture file
simCF <- as.data.frame(simCH)

simCF_XY <- as.data.frame(simCH, fmt="XY")

# Capthist with Trap ID

obsCH_TrapID <- make.capthist(simCF, traps)

# Capthist with xy coordinates

obsCH_XY<- make.capthist(simCF_XY, traps, fmt="XY")

# Plot capture histories
par(mfrow=c(1, 3))
plot(simCH, tracks=TRUE, rad=500)
plot(obsCH_TrapID, tracks=TRUE, rad=500)
plot(obsCH_XY, tracks=TRUE, rad=500)
# Fit models
fit_OG <- secr.fit(simCH, mask=simMask)
fit_TrapID <- secr.fit(obsCH_TrapID, mask=simMask)
fit_XY <- secr.fit(obsCH_XY, mask=simMask)

messages.subject: Re: Problem with as.data.frame [updated] in secr 4.4.4
messages.body_plain:
You've found a bug in the 'as.data.frame' method for capthist objects - detectors were mis-assigned to captures owing to a mis-placed parenthesis in the last release (4.4.4). I don't think it has many other effects, if any.
Thanks for reporting this! A corrected version will be submitted to CRAN in the next few days.

It seems you were generally just playing around. I suggest
popn <- sim.popn(Nbuffer = 20, core = traps, buffer = 2e4, Ndist = "fixed")

messages.subject: openCR groups
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I use openCR 1.4 (I dealt with earlier issues raised here by reverting back to openCR 1.4) to estimate D and phi for a social, warren living species in an 1100ha enclosure.

I no longer get any errors when I use JSSAsecrD models, and if I do I can deal with them by raising the iteration limit.

My question is: should I model both sexes simultaneously or create separate capthist objects for males and females? I know the sexes have different movement patterns across the landscape and we have strong indication that survival rates differ between the sexes. My estimates of D when my capthist includes all individuals with no grouping covariates looks very similar to the output from a capthist that only includes females (see table).

Should I derive total D from the model with no grouping covariate or should I sum the results of my male and female models? Secr.fit generates results that are somewhere in between.

messages.body_plain:
Hi all

I'm having a bit of trouble including a trap-specific time varying covariate in my model and am wondering if anyone can help. At first I though I was inputting the data incorrectly but now I'm unsure because I get the same error when I run the example from the help ('Time-varying Covariates').

Secr.fit produces the beta parameters and AIC etc, but not the fitted parameters and gives the error:

 "Error in secr.lpredictor(formula = models[[x]], newdata = newdata, indx = parindices[[x]],  :  model covariate blockt not found in 'newdata"

I'm unsure what this means as secr.fit seems to recognise 'blockt' in the model up until it tries to estimate the fitted parameters.
Any ideas?

Many thanks
Chris
